theory.title: Exercise 2.3.4: Comparison Operators
theory.content:
⚖️ The Comparison Toolkit

MENTOR-9: "PROTO-7, conditions need tools to test relationships. Is A equal to B? Is X greater than Y? These operators are your measuring instruments."

"Six operators cover every comparison: equality, inequality, greater, less, and combinations."

🔍 Comparison Operators

Equality Operators:

  • ✅ == - Equal to (5 == 5 → TRUE, 5 == 3 → FALSE)
  • ✅ != - Not equal to (5 != 3 → TRUE, 5 != 5 → FALSE)

Relational Operators:

  • ✅ < - Less than (3 < 5 → TRUE, 5 < 3 → FALSE)
  • ✅ > - Greater than (5 > 3 → TRUE, 3 > 5 → FALSE)
  • ✅ <= - Less than OR equal (3 <= 5 → TRUE, 5 <= 5 → TRUE)
  • ✅ >= - Greater than OR equal (5 >= 3 → TRUE, 5 >= 5 → TRUE)

String Comparisons:

  • 🔹 'hello' == 'hello' → TRUE
  • 🔹 'hello' != 'world' → TRUE
  • 🔹 Case-sensitive: 'Hello' != 'hello'

📝 Operators in Action

*** Test Cases ***
Comparison Examples
    ${x}=    Set Variable    10
    ${y}=    Set Variable    20
    ${name}=    Set Variable    Robot
    
    IF    ${x} == 10        # TRUE
        Log    X equals 10
    END
    
    IF    ${x} != ${y}      # TRUE (10 != 20)
        Log    X and Y differ
    END
    
    IF    ${x} < ${y}       # TRUE (10 < 20)
        Log    X less than Y
    END
    
    IF    ${name} == 'Robot'  # TRUE
        Log    Name matches
    END

📋 Comparison Operator Rules

  • 🔹 Numbers: Direct comparison (5 < 10)
  • 🔹 Strings: Must use quotes ('text' == 'text')
  • 🔹 Variables: ${var1} == ${var2}
  • 🔹 Case-sensitive: 'Hello' != 'hello'
  • 🔹 Spacing: Use spaces around operators

🎯 Your Task

Test three different operators: == for equality, != for inequality, <= for range. Master the comparison toolkit!
